etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English armes, from Old French armes, from Latin arma (“weapons”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-mo-, a suffixed form of *h₂er- (“to fit together”), hence ultimately cognate with etymology 2.

definitions.definition: (heraldry) A visual design composed according to heraldic rules, consisting of a coat of arms normally displayed upon an escutcheon, sometimes accompanied by other elements of an achievement

quote.citation: 1950 June, Michael Robbins, “Heraldry of London Underground Railways”, in Railway Magazine, page 382:
quote.text: The Metropolitan Electric trams bore the three seaxes of the Middlesex arms, with a crown above the shield, on a blue circle.

definitions.definition: third-person singular simple present indicative of arm
